nodes.label: Canary Maze UI Spec
nodes.rationale: Ambition L1 deliberately: the data is 2-6 nodes and a handful of text records and the whole value is legibility of evidence read as a still. L2+ actively hurts, because a glowing node graph is exactly the decoy-maze/screensaver reading the critic warned about.

nodes.label: Record Pair (Hero Object)
nodes.rationale: The largest region, sunken so it reads as raw material rather than as our UI, IBM Plex Mono 14/22, every character present with horizontal scroll instead of an ellipsis because hex secrets and IPs are compared character by character. The shared secret is the only marked run of characters on the page, marked identically in both records.

nodes.label: Sequence Figure
nodes.rationale: Compact 160px SVG, contexts as lanes, time left to right, one arc carrying the elapsed time; collapses to '+N more' above six contexts. U-0001 recommends replacing it with a context diff, which is simpler and fixes 320/390 illegibility.

nodes.label: Claim Sentence
nodes.rationale: Public Sans 20/28 500, set as content rather than a hero headline, and states only what the records support.

nodes.label: Scope Limit Line
nodes.rationale: Sits directly under the claim, not in a footnote: a sighting establishes that the secret moved between two request contexts, not that they are two different operators, and cites the measurement that one actor label in the AI Village dump spans 741 addresses. No confidence percentage anywhere.

nodes.label: Verify Bundle Action
nodes.rationale: The one filled vermilion button on the page and the primary action of the whole product; counts real rows while running and expands into the verification strip on pass, or names the failing row while leaving the records intact on fail.

nodes.label: Verification Strip
nodes.rationale: Full-width band stating the Merkle root, rows checked, and the words 'server not contacted'. The demo moment: the claim survives without trusting the operator.

nodes.label: Honesty Footer
nodes.rationale: One line of content with numbers, deliberately not a badge in the top bar: organic sightings, seeded sightings, human requests in ledger 0. Counters roll only when a run adds to them.

nodes.label: Chain-of-Custody Art Direction
nodes.rationale: Derived from the tamper-evident chain-of-custody form: warm document stock canvas, printed near-black ink, serial vermilion accent (the colour a unique serial is printed in on evidence-bag tape), Public Sans as the lettering of official records, IBM Plex Mono for unambiguous 0/O and 1/l/I because secrets are compared character by character.

nodes.label: Screenshot-First Use Scene
nodes.rationale: The canonical artifact is a screenshot pasted into a written submission, so the page is designed to be read as a still image inside a document rather than driven live. Drives the light-only deviation, density 7 with no truncation, and 'Admissible' as the emotional target.

nodes.label: Deviation: Light Only, No Dark Mode
nodes.rationale: Dark-capable was asked for and then derived against: a dark still fights a light document, and the canonical artifact is a screenshot in a written submission. Logged rather than silently dropped.

nodes.label: Deviation: No Card Anywhere on the Page
nodes.rationale: Nothing passes the card test: the records are a homogeneous pair, not a browsable set, and not movable. They get a sunken well instead. No texture, no grain, no grid either, because the records are the texture.

nodes.label: Accent Budget
nodes.rationale: The accent appears in exactly three places (the marker on the shared secret, the Verify button, the focus ring) at under 5% of pixels. --danger is text, word and icon only and never a fill, so form rather than hue distinguishes the two red-family roles. --accent-text exists because #C8361B measured 4.485 on the sunken well, failing 4.5 with no rounding.

nodes.label: Design Tokens
nodes.rationale: Light-only token set with measured contrast ratios annotated per surface, plus precise-personality motion tokens: ease-out-quint, 120-220ms, no bounce.

nodes.label: Five-Second and Thirty-Second Judge Tests
nodes.rationale: At five seconds a stranger must see two monospace records with exactly one identical run of characters marked in both. At thirty seconds the loop completes without narration: markers land, the figure draws, Verify returns a root and 'server not contacted', and the footer states organic versus seeded and zero human requests. One demo-critical screen; everything else is a finished state.

nodes.label: Screen S1: Sighting View
nodes.rationale: The whole product on one route: one sighting, its records, its verification. States: ideal, first-run, partial, error, verified, verify-failed. The three stills that matter are the marked record pair, the verification strip, and the first-run state with the organic counter at 0 — because first-run is the state a judge is most likely to actually see and it must not be embarrassing.

nodes.label: Screen S2: Full Ledger
nodes.rationale: Every mint and sighting row for the reader who wants the rest. A plain table, built last, no flourish; paginates at 20 rows.
